newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-GE expects to double SE Asia sales.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GE expects to double SE Asia sales.

text.p: U.S. giant General Electric Co expects to double its Southeast Asian sales to US$6-7 billion by the year 2000, Kenneth Brown, the president of its Southeast Asia division said on Monday.
Brown told Reuters all the countries in the region had the potential to be billion-dollar markets for the company as governments spent heavily to improve their infrastructure.

"Six to seven billion U.S. dollars in sales is our target for the turn of the century," Brown said in an interview. "I have no doubt at all that we can get there if we execute the way I believe we can."

Brown said whether the company would achieve $6.0 or $7.0 billion in sales by 2000 depended largely on whether its units made acquisitions and the rate at which it agreed future joint ventures in the region. He declined to elaborate.
US-based General Electric makes a range of electrical goods in Southeast Asia from lightbulbs and household appliances such as refrigerators to high-technology aerospace equipment.
The company made sales of $3.4 billion in Southeast Asia last year, or slightly more than four percent of its $79.3 billion worldwide turnover, Brown said.
But the region's contribution to the company's sales and profits was rising as its developing countries boomed.

"Anyone out here with the kind of product scope that we have in the sort of activities that we are in, if they don't have those sorts of targets in mind then they really haven't discovered the growth game. Those sorts of potential are well within grasp," Brown said.
He declined to detail Southeast Asia's past or future profit contributions to the company.

Brown said growth was being driven primarily by the region's fast-paced economic growth and by the fact that General Electric was generally under-represented in its markets, compared to its market share in the West.
Growth was mostly coming from heavy demand for products to improve the region's infrastructure, he said.
"Here in Southeast Asia, two-thirds of our business right now is in the infrastructure game: our power systems business, our aircraft engine business, our transport systems group," he said.
But he said the fastest growing part of General Electric's business was its financial division.

The company's finance group, GE Capital, had become very active in Southeast Asia over the last three years. It had expanded into a range of consumer financing and now accounted for about a fifth of the company's regional turnover, he said.
"Our biggest growth business in GE Capital has been towards the consumer side: auto-financing, credit-cards and hire-purchase plans for consumer appliances and commercial financing," he said.
Geographically, the company expected fast growth in almost every country of the region.

"China has a huge potential for growth," he said. "Its rate of growth will be one of the highest of any area. India will also have a very fast growth rate...in the order of 20 percent a year over the next few years.

"In Southeast Asia, we could see that order of growth in a large number of countries in the region: Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines are all going to see roughly the same rates of growth."
